mainTopic: Which opinion of רבי יהודה stands behind רב's ruling on an animal slaughtered on שבת, and why רב silenced the תנא who recited about cooking on שבת
overview: The גמרא wants to know which ruling of רבי יהודה stands behind רב's statement that an animal slaughtered on שבת may not be eaten that day. A comparison to a lamp lit for שבת is rejected, because the person set the lamp aside with his own hands. רב אשי instead points to the dispute about someone who cooks on שבת. רבי מאיר permits food cooked by mistake. רבי יהודה waits until after שבת. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר allows it after שבת only for others. The גמרא shows that our משנה, which compares שבת to יום הכפורים and calls the slaughter valid for everyone, fits רבי יהודה and not the other two. Next comes a story: a תנא recited before רב that food cooked by mistake may be eaten, and רב silenced him. After rejecting several explanations, רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the תנא was teaching about slaughtering. רבי מאיר permits only food that was already fit to eat raw, not a slaughtered animal. The גמרא challenges this from the scholars' inference that רבי מאיר does permit a slaughtered animal, and it begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The metal lamp source: a lamp lit for this שבת stays forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יהודה's ruling: all metal lamps may be moved on שבת, except a lamp that was lit on that same שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: All metal lamps may be moved, except for the lamp that was lit on that same שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from רבי יהודה that it brought to explain רב's ruling. The quote says that a lamp lit for this שבת may not be moved for that whole שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea being built is this: something that was off-limits when שבת began stays off-limits for the entire שבת. The גמרא wants to apply the same idea to an animal slaughtered on שבת. Because the animal could not be used when שבת started, it would stay forbidden for the whole day.

phrases.english: All metal lamps may be moved,
except for the lamp that they lit
phrases.notes: He means a lamp that was burning when שבת began.

phrases.english: on that same שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source the גמרא brought just before this point to identify which רבי יהודה רב means.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that an animal slaughtered on שבת is forbidden that day
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's ruling that a lamp lit for that שבת may not be moved all שבת

steps.title: The lamp case is different because he set it aside himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison: with the lamp, the person himself pushed it away from use by lighting it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is different there, because he pushed it away from use with his own hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the lamp. It says the lamp case may not be a fair comparison to the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the lamp, the person actively made it off-limits by lighting it. Nobody did anything like that to the animal; it was simply unavailable because it was alive. So רבי יהודה might be strict about the lamp without being strict about the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: And perhaps; introduces a possible rejection
He pushed it away with his own hands; he made it off-limits by his own action

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the animal is not off-limits at the start of שבת. It is only saying that something you made off-limits yourself may be treated more strictly than something that was just unavailable.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
since he pushed it away with his own hands!
phrases.notes: By lighting the lamp, he himself made it unusable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the lamp source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the comparison between the lamp and the slaughtered animal
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lamp was made off-limits by the person's own action, but the animal was not.

steps.title: רב אשי: רב means רבי יהודה's ruling about cooking
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a new source: the dispute about someone who cooks on שבת. רבי מאיר's view comes first: by mistake he may eat it, on purpose he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: it is רבי יהודה's view about one who cooks. We learned: if someone cooks on שבת by mistake, it may be eaten; if on purpose, it may not be eaten. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the lamp proof failed, רב אשי suggests a different ruling of רבי יהודה as the source for רב. He begins by quoting the teaching about cooking on שבת, starting with רבי מאיר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the comparison is between two forbidden acts done on שבת: cooking, and slaughtering an animal. רבי מאיר's view is quoted first so we can see how רבי יהודה is stricter. The next step gives רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier idea and offers a new one
By mistake; without knowing it was forbidden

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
It is Rabbi Yehuda's view regarding one who cooks,
phrases.notes: When רב said "this follows רבי יהודה," this is the ruling he was thinking of.

phrases.english: as we learned: One who cooks on Shabbat,
if by mistake, it may be eaten;
if on purpose, it may not be eaten.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected lamp source with a new source about cooking.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different source of רבי יהודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was relying on רבי יהודה's ruling about the lamp.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was relying on רבי יהודה's ruling about cooking on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even food cooked by mistake waits until after שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that food cooked by mistake may only be eaten after שבת, and food cooked on purpose may never be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if by mistake, it may be eaten after שבת is over; if on purpose, it may never be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the quote with רבי יהודה's stricter view. This is the ruling רב אשי says stands behind רב's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, even a mistaken act on שבת makes the food forbidden for the rest of that שבת. That matches רב's ruling: an animal slaughtered on שבת is forbidden that day. Food cooked on purpose is forbidden forever.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי says רב's ruling comes from רבי יהודה's view about cooking: food made through a שבת violation, even by mistake, may not be eaten on that שבת. The lamp source was rejected because there the person set the lamp aside with his own hands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties רב's ruling about slaughtering on שבת to a general rule: what was produced through a שבת violation is forbidden on that שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
if by mistake, it may be eaten after Shabbat is over;
if on purpose, it may never be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source רב אשי began quoting by giving רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food cooked on שבת by mistake may be eaten only after שבת; food cooked on purpose may never be eaten.

steps.title: The strictest view: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says food cooked by mistake on שבת may be eaten after שבת only by others, and food cooked on purpose may never be eaten by anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says: if he cooked by mistake, the food may be eaten after שבת by other people but not by him. If he cooked on purpose, it may never be eaten, not by him and not by others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the source about cooking on שבת by giving the third and strictest opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר permits food cooked by mistake even on שבת itself. רבי יהודה waits until after שבת. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר goes further: the cook himself may never eat it, and food cooked on purpose is forbidden to everyone forever.

keyTerms.meaning: For other people, but not for the person who cooked it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar says:
By mistake: it may be eaten after Shabbat is over,
by others, but not by him;
on purpose: it may never be eaten,
not by him and not by others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-way dispute that רב אשי brought, after רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By mistake: others may eat it after שבת, but never the one who cooked it. On purpose: forbidden to everyone forever.

steps.title: Why not explain the משנה as on purpose, like רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our משנה (slaughtering on שבת is valid) could not be speaking about someone who slaughtered on purpose, following רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us explain the משנה as talking about someone who slaughtered on purpose, and say it follows רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation that our משנה is about a mistake and follows רבי יהודה. It offers another way to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says food made on purpose may not be eaten on שבת, but it is allowed after שבת. That also fits a משנה that calls the slaughter valid, so why insist on a mistake and רבי יהודה?

keyTerms.meaning: Let us set it up as, explain it as speaking about

phrases.english: But let us set it up as on purpose,
phrases.notes: "It" is our משנה about someone who slaughters on שבת.

phrases.english: and following Rabbi Meir!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the dispute just quoted to suggest a different setup for the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה is about slaughtering by mistake, following רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר also gives a way for the slaughter to count (eating after שבת when done on purpose), so the משנה could just as well follow him.

steps.title: שבת is taught like יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה puts שבת side by side with יום הכפורים. On יום הכפורים no one eats that day, by mistake or on purpose, so on שבת too there must be no eating that day either way. That does not fit רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, because the משנה teaches שבת like יום הכפורים. Just as on יום הכפורים it makes no difference whether it was by mistake or on purpose, he does not eat it, so too here it makes no difference whether by mistake or on purpose, he does not eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion to follow רבי מאיר by pointing to how the משנה is built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים, a fast day, no one eats the meat that day no matter how it was slaughtered. Since שבת is taught the same way, the משנה must hold that on שבת too, even a mistake does not allow eating that day. רבי מאיר lets a mistake be eaten on שבת itself, so the משנה must follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't even think that; it cannot be
Similar to, taught the same way as

steps.confusionAlert: The reason no one eats on יום הכפורים is the fast, not the slaughtering. The גמרא is only learning from the way the משנה groups the two days together.

phrases.english: That cannot enter your mind,
because it is taught like Yom Kippur:
phrases.notes: The משנה lists slaughtering on שבת and on יום הכפורים together.

phrases.english: just as on Yom Kippur

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא בְּשׁוֹגֵג וְלָא שְׁנָא בְּמֵזִיד –
phrases.english: there is no difference whether by mistake and no difference whether on purpose,
he does not eat it,
so too here also,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא בְּשׁוֹגֵג וְלָא שְׁנָא בְּמֵזִיד –
phrases.english: there is no difference whether by mistake and no difference whether on purpose,
he does not eat it.
phrases.notes: He does not eat it that same day. This fits רבי יהודה, not רבי מאיר, who allows a mistake to be eaten right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּקָתָנֵי דֻּמְיָא דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6 and turns down the רבי מאיר reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning from how the משנה groups cases (שבת taught like יום הכפורים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could be about slaughtering on purpose, following רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה treats mistake and on purpose the same for eating that day, which matches רבי יהודה, not רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the order and grouping of a משנה can decide which תנא it follows.

steps.title: But the משנה mentions the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can be about a mistake when it says 'even though he is liable to death,' which only applies to doing it on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really explain it as by mistake, following רבי יהודה? But the משנה says 'even though he is liable with his life'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the reading it just defended, using the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death penalty for breaking שבת only applies to someone who did it on purpose. If the משנה mentions that penalty, it sounds like it is talking about on purpose, not a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable with his life, deserving the death penalty
But look, it teaches... (pointing to wording in the source)

phrases.english: And can you really set it up
as by mistake, following Rabbi Yehuda?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּתְחַיֵּיב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ״ קָתָנֵי!
phrases.english: But it teaches: "even though he is liable with his life"!
phrases.notes: Someone who breaks שבת by mistake is never put to death, so this wording seems to mean on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ בְּשׁוֹגֵג וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading (mistake, רבי יהודה) that step 7 just supported.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה is about slaughtering by mistake.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentions the death penalty, which only comes from doing it on purpose.

steps.title: Reading the death-penalty line correctly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה means: even though slaughtering on purpose would carry the death penalty, here, where it was by mistake, the slaughter is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: even though on purpose he would be liable to death, here, where it was by mistake, his slaughter is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by rereading the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death penalty line is not describing our case. It only tells us how serious slaughtering on שבת is in general. The actual case of the משנה is a mistake, and in that case the slaughter counts.

keyTerms.meaning: His slaughter is valid (the animal is properly slaughtered)

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה is about slaughtering on שבת by mistake and follows רבי יהודה: the slaughter is valid, but the meat is not eaten that day. The death penalty line only describes doing it on purpose.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
even though, on purpose,
he is liable with his life,
here, where it was by mistake,
his slaughter is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning the death penalty means the משנה is about doing it on purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: The death penalty describes doing it on purpose. The משנה's actual case is a mistake, and the slaughter is valid.

steps.title: Why not say the משנה follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה could follow רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, since he also forbids eating that day both by mistake and on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say our משנה follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר. He holds that whether it was by mistake or on purpose, you may not eat it on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes another candidate author for our משנה. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר treats mistake and on-purpose the same on the day itself, which seems to match the comparison to יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the גמרא said the משנה needs an opinion where no one eats that day, by mistake or on purpose. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר fits that rule, so the גמרא asks why we should not say the משנה follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us establish it (say the משנה follows a certain opinion)

phrases.english: And let us establish it according to Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar,
who says: it makes no difference whether it was by mistake
and no difference whether it was on purpose: he may not eat it!
phrases.notes: He means on שבת itself. On that day, both cases are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the משנה is about a mistake and does not fit רבי מאיר, the גמרא proposes רבי יוחנן הסנדלר as its author.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion (steps 3-9) that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר forbids eating that day in both cases, which fits the יום הכפורים comparison. So why not say the משנה follows him?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר allows it only for others
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר allows the food after שבת only for others, while our משנה says the slaughter is valid for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר makes a distinction after שבת: the food is allowed for others but not for him. Our משנה simply says 'his slaughter is valid,' which means it is valid both for him and for others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר does not fully fit our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'his slaughter is valid' with no limits, so even the person who slaughtered may eat the meat. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר forbids the person who did the act to eat it even after שבת, so he cannot be the author.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, meaning the author of our משנה

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדְּלָר קָמְפַלֵּיג בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar makes a distinction after Shabbat ends,
allowing it for others but not for him,
but our Tanna teaches 'his slaughter is valid,'

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא לוֹ וְלָא שְׁנָא לַאֲחֵרִים.
phrases.english: meaning no difference for him and no difference for others.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדְּלָר קָמְפַלֵּיג בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by showing that רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's rule after שבת does not match the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the opinions: the views match on the day itself but differ after שבת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could follow רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, since he forbids eating that day in both cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: It cannot, because the משנה's plain 'valid' allows the meat even for the one who slaughtered, while רבי יוחנן הסנדלר forbids it for him.
steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה cannot follow רבי מאיר (step 7) and cannot follow רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, because 'his slaughter is valid' means valid for everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא recited before רב, and רב silences the reciter
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites before רב that food cooked on שבת by mistake may be eaten and food cooked on purpose may not, and רב silences him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא recited before רב: someone who cooks on שבת by mistake may eat the food; on purpose, it may not be eaten. And רב silenced him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new story connected to the same topic. It sets up the next question: why did רב silence him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling matches רבי מאיר from the earlier steps, who allows food cooked by mistake to be eaten on שבת. רב's silence is the puzzle the גמרא will try to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a reciter who memorized ברייתות and recited them in the study hall

phrases.english: A Tanna recited before Rav:
phrases.notes: Here a תנא is a person whose job was to memorize ברייתות and recite them out loud.

phrases.english: One who cooks on Shabbat,
if by mistake, it may be eaten;
if on purpose, it may not be eaten,
and Rav silenced him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the same cooking-on-שבת rule, this time through a story with רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food cooked on שבת by mistake may be eaten and food cooked on purpose may not. רב silenced the one who recited this.

steps.title: Why did רב silence him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason רב silenced the reciter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason רב silenced him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a plain question about the story. It is setting up a suggested answer, which it will test next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silencing someone means the teacher saw a real problem with what was said. The גמרא wants to find what that problem was.

phrases.english: What is the reason he silenced him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב's action in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was wrong with the ברייתא in רב's eyes, so that he silenced the reciter?

steps.title: Not just because רב holds like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רב silenced him because רב holds like רבי יהודה, but rejects this: you do not silence someone just for teaching another valid opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because רב holds like רבי יהודה while the תנא recited like רבי מאיר, does that make sense? Just because he holds like רבי יהודה, would he silence someone who teaches like רבי מאיר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason and immediately pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's view is a real, respected תנאי opinion. Disagreeing with it is not a reason to stop someone from reciting it, so this cannot explain רב's silence.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: If you say it is because he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
and the Tanna recited like Rabbi Meir,
then just because he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּתָנֵי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר מְשַׁתֵּיק לֵיהּ?!
phrases.english: would he silence someone who recites like Rabbi Meir?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to step 13 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רב silenced the reciter because רב follows רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Disagreeing with a legitimate opinion is not a reason to silence someone who recites it.

steps.title: רב actually rules like רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection: רב does not even hold like רבי יהודה. He rules like רבי מאיר for his students and teaches רבי יהודה's view only in public lectures, because of unlearned people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, does רב even hold like רבי יהודה? But רב חנן בר אמי said: when רב rules for his students, he rules like רבי מאיר. When he gives a public lecture, he teaches like רבי יהודה, because of the unlearned people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger reason why the suggestion fails. רב's real ruling is actually like רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנן בר אמי reports that רב's true ruling follows רבי מאיר, the same view the reciter taught. רב used the stricter view of רבי יהודה only in public, so unlearned people would not treat שבת lightly. So the suggested reason in step 14 is wrong on its facts. The question of why he silenced him is answered in step 17.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב had two different opinions. His true ruling is like רבי מאיר; he taught the stricter view in public only as a safeguard for people who might take שבת lightly.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a sage may teach the public a stricter rule than his true ruling, to protect people who might misuse a lenient rule.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, מִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: And furthermore, does he even hold like Rabbi Yehuda?
But didn't Rav Chanan bar Ami say:
When Rav gives a ruling to his students,
he rules for them like Rabbi Meir,
and when he lectures at the public lecture,
he teaches like Rabbi Yehuda,
because of the unlearned people!
phrases.notes: He worried they might take שבת lightly if they heard that food cooked by mistake may be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, מִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection against the suggested answer in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The basic assumption of step 14 that רב holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב חנן בר אמי's report shows that רב's actual ruling follows רבי מאיר; רבי יהודה's view was only for public lectures.

steps.title: The public lecture idea does not work either
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say רב silenced the תנא because he was teaching in a public lecture, where unlearned people could get the wrong idea. The גמרא rejects this, because the crowd listens to the אמורא, not to the תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the תנא recited this before רב during the public lecture, does everyone listen to the תנא? They listen to the אמורא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא considers one more possible reason for why רב silenced the תנא and pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said רב teaches רבי יהודה's strict view in public lectures because of unlearned people. So one might think רב silenced the תנא to keep the lenient view from the crowd. But the crowd hears only the אמורא, who repeats רב's own words out loud, so the תנא's recitation would not mislead anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: During his public lecture (the big gathering where רב taught the public)
The speaker who repeats the teacher's words loudly to the crowd
Is that to say? (introduces a rejected idea)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: תַּנָּא בְּפִירְקֵיהּ תְּנָא קַמֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: And if you say: the tanna recited it before him during his public lecture,
phrases.notes: The idea is that רב silenced him so the unlearned crowd would not hear the lenient view.

phrases.english: is that to say everyone listens to the tanna?
They listen to the amora!
phrases.notes: The אמורא repeats רב's own words to the crowd, so the people hear רב's ruling, not the תנא's.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא תַּנָּא בְּפִירְקֵיהּ תְּנָא קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off a possible way to save the idea from step 15 that רב's public teaching explains the silencing.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that the public-lecture setting explains why רב silenced the תנא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The crowd hears only the אמורא, who repeats רב, so the תנא's words could not mislead them.

steps.title: The real reason: the case was slaughtering, not cooking
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the תנא was teaching about slaughtering on שבת. רבי מאיר permits only cooked food that was already fit to chew raw before שבת. A slaughtered animal was not fit to eat before, so even רבי מאיר does not permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The תנא taught a case of slaughtering before רב: One who slaughters on שבת by mistake, the meat may be eaten; on purpose, it may not be eaten. רב said to him: Do you think this follows רבי מאיר? רבי מאיר permits only in the case of cooking, since the food was fit to chew raw. But slaughtering, where the animal was not fit to chew, he does not permit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers the question from step 13: why did רב silence the תנא? Because the תנא wrongly applied רבי מאיר's lenient rule to slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reciter's teaching was about slaughtering, not cooking. רבי מאיר's leniency for a mistake works only when the food was already usable before the forbidden act, like raw food that can be chewed. A live animal could not be eaten before it was slaughtered, so the leniency does not apply, and the תנא's version was simply mistaken.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to chew, meaning edible even raw, before the forbidden act

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's leniency for food made on שבת by mistake covers only food that was already edible beforehand, like raw food. It does not cover an animal that was not fit to eat before it was slaughtered.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב rejects רבי מאיר here. רב is saying the תנא stretched רבי מאיר's view to a case רבי מאיר himself never permitted.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
The tanna recited a case of one who slaughters before Rav:
One who slaughters on Shabbat,
by mistake, it may be eaten; on purpose, it may not be eaten.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר?
phrases.english: He said to him: What are you thinking, that it follows Rabbi Meir?

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָשָׁרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir permits it only
phrases.notes: קָשָׁרֵי is two words squeezed together: קא שרי, "he permits."

phrases.english: in the case of one who cooks, since the food was fit to chew,
phrases.notes: Even before cooking, the food could be eaten raw, so it was usable when שבת began.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שׁוֹחֵט דְּאֵין רָאוּי לָכוֹס – לָא!
phrases.english: but one who slaughters, where it was not fit to chew, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק תַּנָּא שׁוֹחֵט תְּנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rejected suggestions in steps 14 to 16, this gives the accepted reason for the silencing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the reciter's teaching was about slaughtering, not cooking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the תנא taught רבי מאיר's valid view on cooking, so silencing him seemed strange.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא wrongly applied רבי מאיר's leniency to slaughtering, which רבי מאיר does not permit, so רב corrected him.

steps.title: Challenge: the scholars inferred that רבי מאיר permits slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this. Our משנה is about slaughtering, and רב taught that the animal is forbidden that day. The scholars said this follows רבי יהודה, which suggests רבי מאיר permits even a slaughtered animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't our משנה about one who slaughters? And רב הונא said: חייא בר רב taught in the name of רב: It is forbidden to eat that day. And the scholars tended to say: This follows רבי יהודה, which implies that רבי מאיר permits it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks step 17's claim that רבי מאיר does not permit a slaughtered animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה is about slaughtering on שבת. רב forbade eating the animal that day, and the scholars said this ruling follows רבי יהודה. That implies רבי מאיר disagrees and permits the slaughtered animal. This contradicts what רב told the תנא in step 17, that רבי מאיר permits only cooked food.

keyTerms.meaning: The group of scholars in the study hall
They tended to, they took up (the view)

phrases.english: But isn't our mishna about one who slaughters?
And Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Ḥiyya bar Rav taught in the name of Rav:
It is forbidden to eat that day,
phrases.notes: "It" is the animal slaughtered on שבת in our משנה.

phrases.english: and the scholars tended to say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר שָׁרֵי!
phrases.english: This follows Rabbi Yehuda, which implies Rabbi Meir permits it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction between cooking and slaughtering that step 17 used for רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that רבי מאיר does not permit eating an animal slaughtered on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב's ruling forbidding the slaughtered animal is said to follow רבי יהודה, then רבי מאיר must permit the slaughtered animal, which contradicts step 17.

steps.title: Starting the answer: when רבי מאיר permits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer by explaining when רבי מאיר permits a slaughtered animal. The answer continues in the next part of the text.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer to the challenge in step 18. It is about to explain in which case רבי מאיר permits a slaughtered animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening words suggest that רבי מאיר does permit a slaughtered animal, but only in a limited situation. That way both step 17 and the implication in step 18 can be true.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Meir permits it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: רבי מאיר's permission applies only in a specific situation (completed in the next part of the text).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 18 implied that רבי מאיר permits a slaughtered animal in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's permission is limited to a specific case, so it does not contradict step 17. The details follow in the next part of the text.
